defect_observations.observation: The body cites Holm pp. 67-68 for the ten-normal example and reports Bonferroni 0.4412670349 and Holm 0.5631999191. The held source prints 0.439 and 0.565 on p. 68 (PDF physical page 5). The treatment neither reports the printed values nor says why its values differ. Phi(3-2.58)^2 = 0.4392 accounts for the printed Bonferroni figure as a rounded-quantile value. A rough Monte Carlo run during this audit (1,000,000 draws) gave 0.5632 +/- 0.001 for Holm, so the text leaves the 0.565 discrepancy unexplained. This audit admits neither figure.

Two parts of the source's power comparison on p. 67 are absent. First, the source claims a strictly larger probability of rejecting false hypotheses except in trivial cases. Second, it explains that the gain is small when all hypotheses are nearly true and large when some are completely wrong, because those are rejected first and the rest face alpha/k for k = n-m, ..., 1. The treatment gives only weak inequalities, the remark 'These inequalities need not be strict', and equality examples. It neither states nor qualifies the source's strictness claim or its account of the gain. The comparison owed by C04 is still present in full.
